claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: MASS alternates evolutionary workflow optimization with supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: To address this, we propose Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS), an RSI method that alternates between evolutionary workflow optimization and supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories.

evidence_spans.source_text: MASS alternates between multi-agent workflow optimization (Algorithms 2) and model fine-tuning that internalizes the workflows (Algorithms 3).

At generation g, the current model L(g) serves as the task-solving agent, workflow optimizer, and evaluator. Algorithm 2 first produces task-specific retained workflows using fixed model weights. Algorithm 3 then generates and self-selects trajectories under these workflows and fine-tunes the same model to obtain L(g+1).

evidence_spans.source_text: This resembles an evolution process with an elite size one (Risi et al., 2026).

The recursive loop here is empirical. Unlike proof-based self-rewriting in Gödel machines (Schmidhuber, 2007), it provides no guarantee that every future cycle improves.

claims.label: partially_supported
claims.claim_summary: Multi-agent traces outperform single-agent training despite using 1.4x fewer tokens.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Moreover, multi-agent traces are also more training-efficient: a student trained on them outperforms a single-agent student trained on 1.4× more training tokens.

evidence_spans.source_text: The first-cycle multi-agent student achieves a 68.3% win rate against the base model, compared with 64.0% for a single-agent student trained on approximately 1.4× more processed supervised tokens (Section 4.4, Figure 6).
More directly, M + reaches 68.3% with 28.82M processed supervised tokens, 4.3 points above S++ while using 31.4% fewer tokens.
M + has broader training-task coverage and a different sampler, so it is not a matched-data control.
These differences in sampling, data, and checkpoint selection limit what can be attributed to teacher composition alone.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Post-training internalizes information-handoff coordination behaviors into model weights.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Finally, trajectory analysis provides evidence that post-training internalizes information-handoff behaviors (Section 5.2).

evidence_spans.source_text: Delegation rises from 1/110 trajectories for L(0) to 48/110 for L(1) and 87/110 for L(2), while code handoffs rise from 1/110 to 42/110 and 83/110, respectively.
These behaviors emerge without providing the optimized workflow at inference time.
Among 114 audited teacher trajectories, 98 contain code handoffs and 57 contain subagent revisions; 79 and 37 of these trajectories, respectively, were sampled for SFT (Appendix G.2).
